lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 3 you met pronouns. Which word can take the place of "Zara" in "Zara ran home"? She: she ran home.
Subject pronouns do the action: I, he, she, we, they. Object pronouns receive it: me, him, her, us, them. Sam and I went. Mum called Sam and me.
A tip: take away the other person. "Mum called me" sounds right, so "Mum called Sam and me".
Intensive pronouns add emphasis: I made it myself. The queen herself arrived. Take them out and the sentence still works.
Unclear pronouns confuse readers: "When Ali met Ben, he laughed." Who laughed? Fix it: "When Ali met Ben, Ben laughed."
Try it in the world: write a note to a friend about a build you made together, using "Kai and I" and "for Kai and me" correctly. Take away Kai to check. Next: commas, brackets and dashes.

exercises.prompt: Choose: "Sam and ___ went to the park."
exercises.explain: "I went", so "Sam and I went".

exercises.prompt: Choose: "Mum called Sam and ___."
exercises.explain: "Mum called me", so "Sam and me".

exercises.prompt: "Myself" in "I made it myself" adds emphasis.
exercises.hint: Take it out: I made it.
exercises.explain: Yes: it is an intensive pronoun.

exercises.prompt: Which one is a subject pronoun?
exercises.explain: "They" does the action.

exercises.prompt: Which one is an object pronoun?
exercises.explain: "Her" receives the action.

exercises.prompt: Which is correct?
exercises.hint: After between, use an object pronoun.
choices: Between you and me, it's a secret.
Between you and I, it's a secret.
exercises.explain: "Between" takes object pronouns: you and me.

exercises.prompt: "When Ali met Ben, he laughed." What is the problem?
exercises.explain: "He" could be Ali or Ben.

exercises.prompt: Choose: "The coach ___ gave us the medals."
exercises.explain: "Herself" is correct; the others aren't standard words.

exercises.prompt: "Him and me built the den" is correct in writing.
exercises.explain: No: "He and I built the den."

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
exercises.explain: "I am ready", so "Zara and I are ready".

exercises.prompt: Leo told Max that he had won; Max was the winner. Which is clearest?
choices: Leo told Max that he had won.
Leo told he that Max won.
exercises.explain: Quoting Leo makes it clear that Max won.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses an intensive pronoun?
choices: The chef herself cooked our meal.
exercises.explain: "Herself" adds emphasis: the chef, and no one else, cooked it.

exercises.prompt: Choose: "The teacher gave the prizes to Nia and ___."
exercises.hint: Take away Nia: gave the prizes to ___.
exercises.explain: "Gave the prizes to me", so "to Nia and me".

exercises.prompt: "Us pupils want a longer break" is correct in formal writing.
exercises.explain: No: "We pupils want a longer break."

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is clearest?
choices: When the cup hit the plate, the plate broke.
When the cup hit the plate, it broke.
It hit it and it broke.
exercises.explain: Naming the plate makes it clear.

exercises.prompt: Sort the pronouns: subject or object?
exercises.hint: Does it do the action (I went) or receive it (called me)?
exercises.explain: I, they and she do the action: subject pronouns. Me, them and us receive it: object pronouns.

exercises.prompt: Match each subject pronoun to its object pronoun.
exercises.explain: I and me; he and him; we and us; they and them.

exercises.prompt: Sort the pronouns: subject, object or intensive?
exercises.hint: Does it do the action, receive it, or add emphasis with -self?
exercises.explain: Subject pronouns do the action: we, they. Object pronouns receive it: him, us. Intensive pronouns add emphasis: herself, myself.

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences: the right pronoun, or the wrong one?
items: Kai and I built a den.
Give it to Zara and me.
exercises.hint: Take away the other person and read it again: 'Mum called I' sounds wrong.
exercises.explain: Right: Kai and I built (I built), to Zara and me (to me), we pupils voted (we voted). Wrong: it should be Mum called Kai and me; Zara and I are late; he and she won.

exercises.prompt: Make "When Ali met Ben, he laughed" clear: Ben laughed. Put the parts in order.
exercises.hint: Keep the start, but name the person instead of saying he.
exercises.explain: When Ali met Ben, Ben laughed. Naming Ben instead of saying he shows exactly who laughed.

exercises.prompt: How many pronouns are in "She told them that we had made it ourselves"?
exercises.hint: Look for every word that stands in for a person or a thing: subject, object and -self words.
exercises.explain: She, them, we, it and ourselves: 5 pronouns. That joins the two parts of the sentence, so here it is not a pronoun.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence to the pronoun that fits its gap.
items: The prize went to Nia and ___.
exercises.hint: Take away the other person, and ask: does it do the action, receive it, or add emphasis?
exercises.explain: Nia and I won (I won). The prize went to Nia and me (to me). I baked the cake myself (emphasis). We pupils want a break (we want).
